_about: Generated places: when a contract, story hook, NPC or travel event needs somewhere to go, a place is made with a name, a pin on the World map and a wiki page (saved when the result is kept). 'contracts' says, per contract type, how often a notice gets a new or reused place, what kind ('settlement', 'industry' or 'site') and how far away in miles. 'reuse' sets how often a nearby generated place is used again instead of a new one. 'styles' are regions: names, architecture, priorities and typical problems, picked by the nearest region page with a nameStyle, else by map box. Industries marked magic are weighted by the region's magic level. Tokens: {name} the place, {anchor} the big place it is near, {goods} what it makes. 'sea' holds places in the water: major and minor ones pinned on the map, and fleeting ones met at sea on journeys.

trees that move in no wind

a pharmacist who sells to anyone, no questions

bone charms said to frighten spawns

plants that grow strange near the spring

masons who must be paid in advance

scorched fences mended weekly

farmers who rarely see the sun

guides who never get lost in fog

ruin.label: ruin
descriptions: Tumbled walls of a manor house, its cellar still intact beneath the rubble.
A roofless chapel whose altar is somehow always free of dust.
The burnt shell of a fortified farm, with arrowheads still in the doorframe.
A collapsed keep whose single standing tower leans over the road.
Foundations of a whole village swallowed by grass, laid out in a perfect circle.
A mansion that was fine fifty years ago and is now home to birds, foxes and worse.
A Magic Society survey post abandoned in a hurry, papers still on the desks.
The ruins of an old temple to a god whose name has been chiselled off every stone.
A ring of broken columns around a sunken courtyard that floods each spring.
An old toll fort, its gate jammed half open for a century.
The remains of a monster-hunters' lodge, its trophy hall now home to the trophies' kin.
A ruined mill whose wheel still turns, though the stream that drove it is gone.
Rows of empty stone houses carved into a cliff face.
A buried city's rooftops showing through the sand.
The shell of a great house, its gardens gone wild and strange with magic.
A crumbling aqueduct that ends in mid-air.
An old border fort with a well that drops further than any rope can reach.
A noble's folly, a half-built tower abandoned when the money ran out.
The ruins of a school for essence users, its practice yards scorched glassy.
A walled graveyard around a ruined church, its gate chained from the inside.

cave.label: cave
descriptions: A sea cave that can only be entered at low tide.
A narrow cleft that opens into a cavern full of glowing fungus.
Caves painted with figures by people long gone, some of them clearly monsters.
A cave mouth that breathes warm air in winter and cold in summer.
A maze of tunnels where the echoes come back wrong.
A cave whose floor is covered in centuries of bones, none of them human.
A flooded cavern with an underground lake as still as glass.
A cave used by smugglers, with rope ladders and a hidden landing.
A cavern where crystals grow from the walls and hum faintly.
A hermit's cave with a carved door and a garden at the entrance.
A cave the locals wall up every winter and open every spring.
A sinkhole cave whose bottom is a forest no sunlight should be able to feed.
A cave where the walls are warm, and something deep below breathes.
A bat colony so vast that their evening flight darkens the sky.
A chain of caves along an old riverbed, with a shrine at each bend.
A cave where lost things turn up, sometimes years later.
A cave under a waterfall, reached by walking behind the falling water.
A cave that the Adventure Society lists as a frequent monster spawn site.
A cave mouth surrounded by ward stones, most of them broken.
A cave whose deepest chamber holds a dead astral space entrance, dark and quiet.

tower.label: tower
descriptions: A slim stone tower with no door at ground level.
An old wizard's tower whose top floor drifts a few inches out of line with the rest.
A signal tower once part of a chain of beacons across the region.
A tower grown, not built, from a single twisted tree turned to stone.
A watchtower over the road with a broken bell and a nest of something large.
A Magic Society observatory, empty, its instruments still turning.
A tower of black glass that reflects the sky a few minutes late.
A lighthouse far from any sea.
A crooked tower whose stairs go up further than the tower is tall.
A prison tower, its cells open and its keys missing.
A ruined tower whose top is crowned with a nest of lightning-scorched stone.
A tower a hermit essence user built to be alone, with a sign that says so.
A tower whose windows glow at night though no one has lived there in years.
A squat tower used by bandits as a lookout.
A tower whose bricks are each carved with a single word, making a long poem.
A tower built around a spring that rises up through its middle.
A tower that rings like a bell when the wind is right.
A tower covered in vines that flower blue in any season.
A tower that the locals say was dropped from the sky.
A half-collapsed tower with a perfectly preserved library on its second floor.

shrine.label: shrine
descriptions: A roadside shrine to the god of travellers, kept by whoever passes.
A grove of standing stones with offerings left at its centre.
A spring said to heal, with crutches hung on the trees around it.
A shrine to a forgotten god, its statue faceless with age.
An altar on a hilltop where pilgrims leave ribbons.
A cave shrine lit by hundreds of candles that never seem to burn down.
A shrine where travellers swear oaths, and broken oaths are said to bring storms.
A tiny chapel built over the grave of a local saint.
A circle of carved trees, each face a different expression.
A shrine to a great astral being, which the churches officially disapprove of.
A shrine at a crossroads with a box for prayers written on scraps.
A spring whose water turns gold at sunset, revered by the locals.
A pilgrims' rest with a small shrine and a well, kept by a lone priest.
A shrine of piled stones that grows a little every year as travellers add to it.
A sunken shrine reached by steps that go down into a pool.
A stone table with a bowl carved into it, always holding rainwater.
A shrine to a beloved local hero, with their weapon set in the stone.
A hidden shrine of a banned church, its symbol painted over and still visible.
A shrine where the bones of a monster are honoured for reasons nobody explains.
A holy tree split by lightning that still blooms every year.

battlefield.label: battlefield
descriptions: An old battlefield where rusted blades still turn up after rain.
A field of grave mounds from a war nobody remembers the reason for.
A hill where a famous last stand happened, marked by a weathered statue.
A plain scarred by essence abilities, with glassy craters and frozen rock.
A battlefield where the grass grows red.
The site of a great surge defence, with collapsed earthworks and broken ward stones.
A field where the dead are said to march on the anniversary of the battle.
A valley full of rusted siege engines left to rot.
A battlefield where a monster of Silver rank was brought down, its bones still lying there.
A field the farmers will not plough.
A hill crowned with a cairn of helmets.
A trench line overgrown with flowers.
A burned wood where the trees are still charcoal black after decades.
A field marked with hundreds of small cairns, one for each fallen.
A plain where arrows still stick out of the earth at odd angles.
A ford where a famous ambush happened, the banks lined with bones.
A field where two great houses fought and both claim to have won.
A shallow valley where a duel between two Gold-rankers reshaped the land.
A battlefield turned pilgrimage site, with a small inn for visitors.
A battle site where a monster horde was stopped, marked by a wall of fused stone.

waystation.label: waystation
descriptions: A lonely inn at a crossroads, run by a family who never seems to age.
A walled waystation for caravans, with a well and a smith.
An inn built into an old fort, with arrow slits for windows.
A roadhouse famous for its stew and its brawls.
A pilgrims' hostel with a bell that rings when someone is near.
A coaching inn where the horses are better fed than the guests.
A rest house on stilts above a flood plain.
An inn that serves only adventurers, by long-standing rule.
A ferry inn where the landlord also works the ferry.
A desert waystation built around a deep cistern.
An inn with a famous signboard that people come miles to see.
A toll house turned tavern, still charging a toll for the bridge.
A mountain hut with blankets, firewood and an honesty box.
A ramshackle inn run by a retired Bronze-ranker with one arm.
A great barn of an inn where drovers sleep alongside their herds.
An inn where every guest must leave a story in the book.
A lodge that offers Adventure Society members free beds.
A haunted inn whose ghost is part of its trade.
A riverside tavern that floods every spring and reopens every summer.
A waystation run by the Church of the Journey, open to all.

bandit-camp.label: bandit camp
descriptions: A camp hidden in a ravine, its approach watched from the rocks.
A ruined farm turned bandit hideout, its windows boarded.
A cave hideout behind a waterfall.
A palisade camp in the marsh reached only by hidden paths.
A camp of deserters who still wear the uniforms they abandoned.
A treetop camp linked by rope bridges.
A hideout in an old mine, with traps on the approach.
A camp disguised as a charcoal-burners' clearing.
A fortified ruin with a sentry who sings when travellers come.
A sunken ship in a cove used by smugglers and worse.
A camp led by a disgraced Iron-ranker who still keeps the Society's rules, sort of.
A camp moving every few days, its trail cleverly hidden.
A hideout in a cellar under an abandoned inn.
A camp of desperate villagers driven off their land.
A camp at an oasis that charges caravans for water.
A hideout in a hollow hill reached through a fox den.
A camp with a captured monster chained as a guard.
A camp that runs a fake toll on the road.
A camp hiding in a burned forest, smeared in ash.
A hideout in a fallen tower, its stairs trapped.

lair.label: monster lair
descriptions: A nest of crushed reeds and bones in the marsh.
A burrow under a hill, with gnawed trees all around.
A den in a cave, its entrance marked with claw scratches.
A tangle of webs between dead trees, glittering with dew.
A wallow in a mud flat surrounded by the remains of meals.
A rookery of something large on a cliff.
A nest in an abandoned watchtower.
A den in the roots of a huge tree, the ground torn up all around.
A sunken lair in a flooded quarry.
A hive built into a ruined house, humming.
A lair in a collapsed mine, with eggs in the dark.
A nest of scorched stone where the ground is warm.
A ring of trampled grass where the herd gathers at night.
A cliff-face of burrows that whistle in the wind.
A pool where something lies just under the surface.
A den guarded by a dozen lesser spawns.
A nest built from stolen goods, including a cart.
A thicket of thorns grown thick by something living inside it.
A lair in a ruined shrine, the altar used as a sleeping place.
A lair near a spawn point, where new monsters keep joining the pack.

dungeon.label: dungeon entrance
descriptions: A sinkhole in a field revealing carved stonework below.
A stair cut into the hillside that leads down into darkness.
A vault door set into a cliff, sealed with a ward nobody can read.
A collapsed barrow, its passage open for the first time in centuries.
A well that opens into a huge chamber halfway down.
A mine shaft that broke into older tunnels nobody dug.
A ring of stones around a hole with no bottom.
A temple stair half buried in sand.
A cellar door in an empty field.
An entrance revealed when the lake dropped in a drought.
A stable astral space entrance marked with Adventure Society flags.
A crypt beneath a ruined chapel, its gate rusted open.
A crack in the earth after a quake, breathing warm air.
An ancient gate carved into the mountain, cold and silent.
A hidden entrance under the roots of a fallen tree.
A dry riverbed that ends in a tunnel.
A vault beneath a ruined tower, its door scratched from the inside.
A drowned stair leading under the sea, uncovered at the lowest tides.
A circle of black stone slabs that slide apart at the right word.
A pit where the Magic Society's instruments go wild.

quirks: Every door in {name} is painted blue, and nobody can agree why.
The well in the square gives water that tastes faintly of mint.
Children here learn to count by the bells of the shrine, not on their fingers.
Strangers are offered bread and salt at the boundary stone, and refusing is a grave insult.
The headman is chosen each spring by a goat, which is led through the crowd until it stops.
Half the roofs are thatched with reeds from the marsh and the other half with old cart canvas.
A retired Bronze-ranker runs the only inn and tells the same three stories every night.
There is a statue in the square of a hero nobody remembers, and its nose is rubbed bright for luck.
Everyone keeps a pair of iron scissors over the door against things that come at night.
The local dogs refuse to cross the old bridge, so the people of {name} carry them over.
Market day is every ninth day, and the whole place counts its week by it.
The tavern sign has been stolen so many times that it is now chained, padlocked and warded.
People here name their children after the weather on the day they were born.
A feud between two families over a boundary hedge has run for four generations.
The shrine bell rings by itself during monster surges, a few hours before the spawns come.
Every house has a small clay figure on the windowsill, and they are turned to face the road when someone dies.
The village keeps a ledger of every traveller who has passed through, going back two hundred years.
Nobody in {name} whistles after dark.
The children run a betting ring on how long each new adventurer will last.
A single enormous tree grows in the middle of the main street, and the road simply goes around it.
The local brew is made with honey and something bitter nobody will name.
The people here are proud of {goods}, and will compare everyone else's unfavourably.
Every wedding ends with the couple jumping over a fire, then into the river.
The village elder is a woman of a hundred and four who claims a Silver-ranker owes her a favour.
The town crier announces gossip as well as news, and is the most feared person in {name}.
Spirit coins are rarely seen here; most trade is barter in {goods}.
Graves are dug in the hillside facing the road, so the dead can see who visits.
A traveling preacher of the Church of the Journey stopped here forty years ago and never left.
There is a standing fine for anyone who mentions the old mayor by name.
Everyone in {name} keeps chickens, including the priest, the smith and the drunk.
The roads are paved with broken pottery, so the whole place crunches underfoot.
A broken monster core sits in the shrine as a relic, and people leave copper coins beside it.
Visitors are expected to carve their initial into the gatepost; it is bad luck to leave without doing it.
The local lord has not visited in eleven years, and the village has quietly stopped paying his taxes.
There is a contest each harvest to grow the largest gourd, and cheating is endemic.
The headman's office is an upturned boat on the green.
Everybody here is related to everybody else, and they will explain exactly how at length.
People leave a lamp burning on the edge of {name} each night for travellers who never arrived.
The inn serves the same stew every day, and it has been simmering, topped up, for nine years.
Births are celebrated by planting a fruit tree, so the orchard is a map of the village's families.
A pair of rival healers practise on opposite sides of the street and slander each other cheerfully.
No one here locks their doors, and newcomers who do are quietly distrusted.
Everyone in {name} carries a small knife, including children, and uses it for eating.
The local tongue drops half its consonants, and folk from {anchor} complain they can't understand a word.
An old adventurer's armour hangs in the square, and children dare each other to try on the helmet.
The village has a resident cat population larger than its human one, and the cats are fed by law.
The shrine has been rededicated to three different gods in living memory, and still bears all three symbols.
Water is drawn from the river by a great wheel that groans loud enough to hear a mile off.
Every season, the young people walk the boundary at night carrying torches to keep the old agreements.
A painted sign at the edge of {name} lists the monsters spotted that year, with tallies.
Locals wear a sprig of a particular herb in their hats to show which family they belong to.
Arguments are settled by a public game of stones on the inn's front step.
The miller is also the magistrate, the tax collector and the only person who can read.
Folk here say grace to the rain, not to any god.
There is a narrow tower at the edge of {name} with a lookout on duty at all hours.
The houses are built half underground to keep cool, and their roofs are covered in grass.
Every family keeps a jar of earth from the place their ancestors came from.
An enormous monster skull serves as the village gate.
People in {name} greet each other by asking after the health of their animals before their families.
No wagon may enter the square on market day; goods are carried in by hand.
Ever since a famous wedding feast, the inn has insisted on charging adventurers double.
The local priest gives sermons in rhyme, badly.
A small Adventure Society noticeboard hangs outside the inn, usually covered in drawings by children.
The whole place smells of {goods}, and visitors stop noticing after a day.
Every house has a bench outside it, and the evening is spent sitting on them, talking across the road.
Lost property is hung on a big wooden frame in the square until it is claimed or rots.
There is a rope across the river and a raft that anyone may use, but it must be left on the side you found it.
The young men and women race up the hill each spring, and the winner speaks for {name} for a year.
A circle of standing stones by the fields hums faintly when touched.
The village is famous for its pies, which are mostly gravy.
Swearing is fined, and the fines pay for the festival, so the festival is very well funded.
The local militia drills on the green every sixth morning with spears older than they are.
The people here keep bees in the walls of their houses, and the walls hum in summer.
Funerals are cheerful, and weddings are solemn, and nobody here sees why outsiders find that odd.
There is a famous local storyteller who will only perform if paid in sweets.
Everyone who passes the shrine touches a smooth stone set in its wall; it has been worn into a hollow.
Buildings are painted with eyes above the doors to keep out spirits.
A wandering astral space entrance once opened near {name}, and locals still talk about what came out.
The community hall is built from the hull of a ship, though the nearest sea is far away.
Every inhabitant over twelve knows how to set a bone and stitch a cut.
The place has two names, one used by the old families and one by everyone else.
Lanterns here burn a pale green from an oil pressed from local seeds.
There is no inn; travellers are assigned to households by lot.
The people of {name} hold a feast every year to celebrate surviving the last surge.
The headman wears a chain of office made from monster teeth.
Every gate and fence post is topped with a carved bird, each one different.
A local tradition says every visitor must answer a riddle before eating; most locals just give them the answer.
There is a public bathhouse fed by a warm spring, and most business is done there.
The children chalk maps of the surrounding land on the walls, and they are surprisingly accurate.
A dispute over who owns the village's only cow has been in court in {anchor} for six years.
People here believe it is unlucky to say the number seven, and count six, six-and-one, eight.
Every window has a small mirror hung outside it, angled toward the road.
The town clock has run eleven minutes slow for a century and the town keeps its time.
The inn's cellar is an old crypt, and the wine racks stand between the tombs.
Every wall is plastered with notices about lost goats.
A sullen ex-soldier runs a fencing school in the barn and has two students.
Instead of a temple, {name} has a long table where any god's priest may preach on their day.
Bread here is baked in a communal oven, and each family marks its loaves with a stamp.
Ever since an essence user grew a garden overnight, the people expect magical help with the harvest.
The people here eat lizards, and are offended when visitors don't.
The best-dressed person in {name} is the gravedigger.
Shoes are taken off at every threshold, including the shrine and the smithy.
The village dog is officially on the council and has a seat at meetings.
Fires are forbidden after midnight since the great blaze, and a warden walks the lanes checking.
Every local family claims descent from an outworlder, and none can prove it.
There is a contest each winter to see who can tell the biggest lie, judged by the priest.
The road into {name} is lined with cairns, one for each person lost to monsters.
Every building has a ladder to the roof, because in floods everyone goes up.
Debts are recorded by notching sticks that hang in the inn, and are paid off on feast days.
The local midwife is also a fortune-teller, and gives every baby a fortune at birth.
The people here sing while they work, and the songs are long, rude and very old.
Most of the houses are built on stilts, and the space beneath is used for goats.
No one has been allowed to cut the great hedge around {name} since a promise made to a passing druid.
Coins from distant countries are nailed to the inn's beams, one for every traveller who came from farther away than the last.
There is a statue of a monster in the square, carved to look friendly, as a mascot.
Everyone here takes a nap after the midday meal and the place goes silent.
A team of retired Iron-rankers serves as the local watch and argues constantly about tactics.
Water is precious here, and guests are measured a cup on arrival and asked to return what they don't drink.
The local ale is so strong that the inn forbids anyone to drink more than two before a fight.
An old wizard's house stands empty in the middle of {name}, and everyone walks around it.
The village measures distance in 'pipes' — how far you walk while smoking one.
Rival bakers produce a sweet and a savoury loaf respectively, and the village is divided down the middle.
Every child is given a wooden sword at seven, and the sword is burned on their wedding day.
Visitors are expected to bring news, and the inn gives a free meal for the best story.
Every gate has a little bell, so the whole place jingles with comings and goings.
The people of {name} don't trust spirit coins and store their wealth in salt.
An enchanted weathervane on the shrine points toward the nearest monster, not the wind.
The local guard captain is fourteen years old and terrifyingly competent.
All the dogs in {name} are descended from one enormous hound, and they all look exactly alike.
People here use their mothers' names as surnames, and are baffled by other customs.
There is a regular market for monster parts, and the butcher is unusually knowledgeable.
A crumbling wall surrounds {name}, older than any record, and nobody knows who built it.
Locals keep a special pot of soup simmering for the god of travellers, and any guest may eat from it.
The council meets in a hollow tree big enough for twelve chairs.
Every season, a stranger with no shadow visits for one night and buys a drink, and nobody questions it.
There is an annual race on the river in barrels, and broken bones are considered part of the fun.
People in {name} believe that ringing a bell during a storm drives off lightning, and ring constantly.
Every resident takes a turn on the night watch, and grumbles about it at length.
A lost cart full of {goods} once fed {name} through a famine, and the cart wheel is kept as a relic.
The local healer will only treat those who can tell her a joke she hasn't heard.
Anyone who kills a monster within sight of {name} is owed a free drink for life, and the inn keeps a list.
The priest and the innkeeper are married and run their businesses from the same building.
Smoke from the chimneys here is faintly coloured because of the dyes used in local fuel.
The roads in {name} are named after the people who were run over on them.
There is a monthly public reading of the law, which takes most of the day and is well attended for the gossip.
The village keeps a pet monster, a harmless Iron-rank lizard the size of a dog, in a pen by the inn.
Everyone here has a nickname, and real names are only used at funerals.
An Adventure Society plaque by the gate records the day {name} survived a surge with no deaths.
Wells here are blessed every spring by the Church of the Healer, and the blessing is a festival.
Every family has a symbol painted on its door, and the symbols are used instead of house numbers.
There is a bridge here built by an earth-essence user in a single afternoon, and it has no visible supports.
The tavern keeps a 'quiet room' where anyone may sit without being spoken to.
People in {name} eat their main meal at dawn and only bread after noon.
A sealed jar of earth from {anchor} sits in the shrine, and is opened only when someone leaves for good.
The local smith makes knives with a curious ripple in the blade, and won't say how.
At the end of each year everyone throws one possession they no longer want into the river.
Every house has a small garden of the same herb, which the locals swear keeps the ague away.
The square is shaded by a vast awning of sewn sails, repaired by everyone each spring.
People here use a different calendar from the rest of the region, and are a few weeks out of step.
A small library sits above the stables, and it is the pride of {name} with forty-three books.
Nobody here takes payment for directions, but they'll take a story.
A collapsed watchtower has been converted into a dovecote, and the birds carry messages to {anchor}.
The road through the middle of {name} is so rutted that locals keep planks to lay over the worst bits.
People here wear their hair long until they've done something brave, then crop it.
An elderly Celestine is rumoured to live quietly in {name}, and the locals protect her privacy fiercely.
There is a weekly dance in the barn, and the musicians are terrible and beloved.
Every resident owns a lantern of the same design, all made by one family.
Toll collection on the road is done by a very polite goose, and nobody can explain how it works.
The village fool is actually a retired Silver-ranker who enjoys the quiet.
Locals greet outsiders by asking which god they serve, and judge them accordingly.
The inn has a bed that once held a famous adventurer, and it costs triple to sleep in.
Every house has a bucket of sand by the door, and the fire drills are a beloved spectacle.
Mothers here tell their children that the Adventure Society takes naughty children away, so the children fear adventurers.
Every year, a mock trial is held for the weather, and it is always found guilty.
There is a curious echo in the main street, which repeats words a few seconds late.
People here measure wealth in sheep, even those who own none.
Grain is stored in an old monster's shell, which keeps out rats entirely.
A stone circle in the square serves as the village calendar and sundial.
Most locals have never been to {anchor} and are faintly suspicious of it.
Every guest is asked to plant a seed before they leave, and the hedgerows are wildly varied.
The headman has a powerful voice and conducts business by shouting from his roof.
There is a tradition of public apologies, delivered from a small stage by the well.
Children here play 'surge', a game where some are monsters and the rest are adventurers.
Every inhabitant is required to keep one weapon by law, and most keep a pitchfork.
The shrine's priest is blind and knows everyone by their footsteps.
The only shop sells everything from rope to wedding dresses, and the owner remembers what everyone owes.
Wooden charms shaped like fish hang from every eave, even far from water.
There is an ancient treaty with a nearby monster, and the villagers leave it a goat every season.
Nobody in {name} can agree whether the river is lucky or cursed, so they thank it and curse it in the same breath.
Local folk celebrate the anniversary of a bad harvest instead of a good one, to remember humility.
A tame awakened crow lives in the inn and repeats gossip, accurately.
An old essence user's stone circle stands in the field, and crops grow twice as tall within it.
The weekly market includes a stall where anyone can swap a secret for a secret.
Every newborn is weighed against a sack of {goods} and the sack is given as a gift.
The people of {name} paint the fronts of their houses each spring, and argue for months about colours.
There is a carved post in the square where anyone can nail up a grievance, and the headman must answer each one.
Every evening, someone climbs the hill and lights a beacon to say all is well; a dark beacon means danger.
The inn keeps a board of wanted notices, and some of the faces have been there for decades.
There are more shrines here than houses, each to a different small god or ancestor.
Ancient roads cross {name}, and the stones are marked in a script nobody can read.
People here keep their savings in hollowed-out books, and everyone knows it.
The village mascot is a giant wooden duck, wheeled out on feast days.
The local magistrate rules by consulting an old coin, and the coin has never been wrong, according to the magistrate.
There is a ferocious rivalry with the next village over about whose festival is older.
Every resident wears a bead bracelet, one bead for each year they've lived in {name}.
The place was rebuilt after a fire, and every building is exactly the same, which confuses visitors.
The well is guarded by an elderly woman with a crossbow, who charges a copper per bucket to outsiders.
Every hearth in {name} was lit from one fire, carried from {anchor} a century ago, and it has never been allowed to go out.
Locals greet each other with a wave of three fingers, and the meaning is long forgotten.
The local brewer infuses ale with essence-touched herbs, and its effects are unpredictable.
People here hold that dreams are messages from the dead, and discuss them over breakfast.
Every carpenter in {name} leaves one deliberate flaw in each piece of furniture for luck.
The town's banner shows a monster being kicked by a farmer, based on a true story.
A small, well-kept garden memorialises a beloved mule.
Every visitor is given a stone to carry while in {name}, and must return it when they leave.
There is a single, ancient lamppost in the middle of {name} that has never needed oil.
Shopkeepers here hang a broom outside to show they are open and turn it upside down when closed.
The best fighter in {name} is the baker, who has driven off three monsters with a peel.
A traditional dance here imitates the movements of a monster, and is performed with great seriousness.
Food is shared on a long common table in the square, and eating alone is considered rude.
Every house keeps a ladder to its neighbour's roof, a custom from the floods.
The local stories say a great astral being once slept on the hill, and the grass there grows in a spiral.
People here believe mirrors steal luck, so there are none, and everyone looks slightly unkempt.
An old Magic Society survey marker stands in the square, and children climb it.
The village kitchen garden is tended by everyone, and stealing vegetables is punishable by more gardening.
There is a strong tradition of hospitality to adventurers, born of gratitude for a rescue long ago.
Every season, a merchant from {anchor} comes to buy {goods}, and the whole place puts on a show.
The sign at the edge of {name} has been altered by pranksters so many times that no one is sure of the real name.
The people of {name} hold their meetings in silence, voting with stones dropped in jars.
A crumbling chapel to a forgotten god is maintained by an order of exactly one monk.
There is a hot spring under the inn, and its floors are always warm.
The local schoolteacher was once a scholar in {anchor} and lectures the children on astral geometry.
Locals keep a ledger of every monster spawn, with dates and sizes, going back eighty years.
Every resident has a ritual phrase they say when leaving the boundary, and no two are the same.
There is a 'debt tree' where people tie ribbons for favours owed.
Weddings in {name} last a full week and bankrupt everyone involved.
Every home keeps a small essence-lamp, a gift from a Magic Society survey long ago, though most have dimmed.
An earnest young priest is trying to start a choir and has recruited mostly goats.
Every house in {name} has a name, and the names are much grander than the houses.
A once-famous racehorse lives out its days in the paddock and is visited like a celebrity.
There is an underground cellar network beneath {name}, connected for safety during surges.
The village council is made up of whoever turns up, and decisions are made by those who stay longest.
An old stone marks the farthest point a monster has ever reached into {name}, and kids dare each other to touch it.
People here salt their tea, and are amazed others don't.
The fields around {name} are marked with stones painted different colours for each family.
There is a running feud with a band of awakened rabbits in the hills, and the rabbits are winning.
Everyone here owes the innkeeper money, and so does the innkeeper.
Locals tell visitors that the hill to the north is haunted, mainly to keep them away from the best berries.
There is a woman in {name} who claims to be four hundred years old and certainly acts like it.
The people of {name} keep a small stuffed monster in the inn, which they move around to scare newcomers.
An adventurer's sword is stuck fast in a rock by the river, and anyone may try to pull it out for a copper.
Locals celebrate when a monster core is found in {name}, and display it before selling it in {anchor}.
There is a flock of half-wild geese that patrols {name} more effectively than the watch.
The children learn their letters from carved signs that tell the local history.
People in {name} always leave one seat empty at the table for the dead.
The inn's ceiling is covered in the signatures of every adventuring team that ever stayed.
The village has a law, still enforced, against riding a horse backwards on the green.
A local craftsman builds tiny models of every house, and the model village sits in the inn's window.
There is a famous local recipe that uses a monster part as a spice, and it is not for the faint of heart.
The bell in the shrine was cast from melted armour after a battle long ago.
Every farm in {name} has a scarecrow dressed as an adventurer, and they get more elaborate every year.
Locals keep cats in the granaries and dogs in the houses, and anyone who swaps them is shunned.
There is a spring here whose water makes people briefly honest, and the locals use it to settle disputes.
A great flat rock serves as the village stage, and anyone may perform on it on feast nights.
The people of {name} trade in favours rather than coin, and keep careful mental tallies.
There is a small museum of things found in the fields, mostly arrowheads and one very confusing helmet.
Every autumn the whole place turns out to herd the wild pigs out of the orchards with drums.
An outworlder lived here years ago and taught everyone a card game, which is now played obsessively.
Visitors must sign the inn's guest book, which is chained to the bar and thicker than a temple ledger.
The well-water is so cold it hurts, and locals compete to see who can drink a cup fastest.
Every house in {name} faces east, toward the sunrise, even when that means facing away from the road.
The shrine has a box where people leave anonymous confessions, and the priest reads the best ones aloud.
There is a long-running wager in the inn about when the old bridge will finally collapse.
Everyone in {name} keeps a pet of some kind, and the pets are brought to council meetings.
The local festival involves throwing rotten fruit at a straw effigy of a tax collector.
There is a small Church of the Hearth hall here that doubles as the village kitchen.
Every child born during a surge is said to be lucky, and they are treated with mild reverence.
A pair of stone lions guards the road into {name}, and one has been repaired with a very different head.
People here refuse to eat fish for reasons they won't explain to outsiders.
The village is known for its swing bridge, which sways and creaks but has never failed.
Every new resident must plant a hedge, and the hedges have grown into a maze around the edges.
An old woman sits at the crossroads and asks every traveller where they're going, then tells them the way is wrong.
The headman's house is the smallest in {name}, by tradition, so that power stays humble.
The inn's best room has a window painted onto the wall, because the real one was bricked up after a monster came through it.
Folk here refuse to sell anything on the first day of the month, and give it away instead.
The local guard wear armour patched together from at least four different eras.
Everyone in {name} has a garden gnome carved in the likeness of a family member.
A wandering bard once wrote a song mocking {name}, and the locals sing it louder than anyone.
The bakery opens at midnight and closes at dawn, and the baker has never been seen in daylight.
The village has a resident awakening-stone collector who will trade stories for a look at yours.
Lamps along the main street are lit by a child who earns a copper a night and takes it very seriously.
Every fence in {name} is built from salvaged wagon wheels.
The shrine keeps a jar of every kind of soil from places its pilgrims have visited, labelled in tiny writing.
The local apothecary sells cures for everything, labelled honestly as 'probably useless'.
A pack of dogs follows every adventurer who enters {name} until they leave, as if escorting them.
There is a tradition of leaving a coin in a crack in the bridge for each safe crossing, and the bridge is rich.
The miller's wheel is turned by a tame monster instead of water, and it eats a whole sheep a week.
Everyone in {name} keeps their front door open in daytime, and a closed door means someone is ill.
People here bow to the river every morning, and the custom has outlived whatever god it honoured.
The village's only clock is a sundial in the square, and on cloudy days nobody knows the time and nobody minds.

settlement: The headman has been selling the village's grain to smugglers and blaming the shortage on rats.
A cult of the Church of Purity meets in the cellar of the inn every new moon.
The well is fed by a spring that rises from a sealed astral space, and its magic is slowly changing the children.
The village was founded by deserters, and their descendants still fear the army will come for them.
The local priest is an outworlder hiding what she is.
The beloved old healer is poisoning someone slowly, and has done it before.
A noble house in {anchor} secretly owns every field here through a front man.
The village pays a monster in the hills to leave them alone, and it is asking for more.
Half the village are members of a smuggling ring, and the other half pretend not to know.
The founder's tomb holds a Bronze-rank monster core, never sold, worth more than the whole village.
The headman's son is an essence user who has never registered with the Adventure Society.
A body is buried under the floor of the inn, and three people know whose it is.
The village's famous {goods} is adulterated, and a merchant in {anchor} is about to find out.
The innkeeper is an informant for a criminal syndicate in {anchor}.
The children have found a cave full of awakening stones and told no adult.
The village's founder made a deal with something that still comes to collect every fifty years, and it is nearly time.
The miller is a retired assassin who just wants to be left alone.
A family here are secretly Celestines, and they will do anything to keep it hidden.
The village shrine is dedicated to a god that the churches consider outlawed.
Someone here is spying for a rival noble house and sending reports by pigeon.
The well-loved village elder is the reason the last headman disappeared.
An old treaty says the land belongs to a tribe who are coming to reclaim it.
The village guard captain takes bribes to look the other way when slavers pass.
The tavern's cellar connects to old tunnels that run under the whole village.
The local magistrate has been forging land deeds for years.
A sickness is spreading quietly, and the healer is hiding it to keep the market open.
The village's only essence user is losing control of their power.
The blacksmith has been making weapons for a bandit gang in exchange for protection.
A child here was born with a strange mark and the family is hiding them from the priests.
The village is built over a ley line, and the Magic Society wants to move everyone out.
The innkeeper waters the ale with something that makes people talk too freely.
A local hero's famous deed was actually done by someone else, who is still alive and bitter.
The village's patron saint was a con artist, and an old diary proves it.
Someone has been stealing monster cores from the hunters' catches.
A wealthy widow is planning to buy up every house and evict the families.
The local priest has lost his faith and keeps preaching out of habit and fear.
Two leading families are planning a marriage to merge their land, and the bride has other plans.
The headman has an illegitimate child in {anchor} who will inherit everything.
A merchant here sells cursed trinkets to travellers on purpose.
The village's prized relic is a fake; the real one was sold decades ago.
The local watch is armed with weapons stolen from an Adventure Society shipment.
A respected farmer is a monster in human shape, and has been for years.
Someone here sends messages to a cult, using the washing lines as a code.
The village's water is laced with a mild essence-tainted herb that keeps everyone calm.
The old woman everyone thinks is mad is the only one who knows what really happened in the last surge.
A local family has been hiding a wounded Silver-rank monster, believing it a god.
The new priest is not a priest at all, and fled {anchor} after a murder.
The village was paid by a noble house to stay quiet about what they saw on the road.
Someone is digging at night in the old graveyard, and finding things.
The tax ledger sent to {anchor} is pure fiction, and has been for twenty years.
The village's best tracker is leading travellers into ambushes.
The local alchemist is brewing something for the Magic Society that they've been told is harmless.
A runaway noble is hiding here under a false name, and her family has hired hunters.
The shrine bell's warning before surges is a trick by the priest, who reads Society reports.
The village has two headmen, one public and one who truly decides.
The orchard's best fruit grows over a mass grave.
A local boy has been talking with something in the woods, and it has been teaching him magic.
The village elder signed a contract with a mining company that will flood the valley.
A group of villagers plans to burn the house of a family they blame for a death.
The innkeeper keeps a ledger of every guest's secrets, and sells them.
site: Something is living in the lowest level, and it is not a monster but a person who never left.
A hidden room holds the journal of the last people here, explaining why they left.
The place is a spawn point that is building towards a surge.
A cache of Bronze-rank awakening stones is hidden behind a loose stone.
The ruin is a decoy; the real treasure is buried a hundred paces east.
A cult has started using it for rituals, and their circles are still drawn on the floor.
The site sits on a dormant astral space entrance that is beginning to wake.
Bandits have been using it as a drop point, and their stash is still here.
The bones here belong to an adventuring team the Society listed as missing.
The site was sealed by the Magic Society for a reason they have forgotten.
Whoever enters at night hears their own voice calling from deeper inside.
A forged deed claims the site for a noble house who want what is under it.
A wounded monster has made its den here, and it is clever enough to set traps.
There is a second entrance, used by smugglers, that nobody else knows about.
An old ward keeps something sealed below; the ward is failing.
A treasure map carved into a wall leads to another site in the region.
An essence user died here, and their essences crystallised in the stone.
A rival adventuring team plans to clear the site first and claim the reward.
The site is haunted by a spirit that will trade knowledge for a favour.
An artefact here makes anyone who holds it hear thoughts nearby.
Something buried here is calling monsters to the area.
The site is the old border marker in a land dispute, and moving one stone would change who owns the valley.
A trapped and starving monster in a pit below is a rare Silver-rank creature.
A sealed coffin holds a living person in enchanted sleep.
A wall painting shows the region's future, and some of it has come true.
The place's guardian is a construct that still follows orders from a dead master.
The site is a meeting point for spies from two rival houses.
A collapsed passage hides the bodies of the last explorers and their maps.
The place is the only source of a rare reagent the Magic Society badly needs.
A child's toy lies in the deepest chamber, untouched by dust, every time.
The stones here are marked with a map to an even older place.
The whole site is an illusion over something much worse.
A false floor hides a drop into an underground river.
The site was used by the Church of Purity to imprison people before its fall.
The local legend is backwards: the monster was the guard, and the treasure the danger.
A family heirloom stolen from {anchor} is hidden here.
Someone has been leaving food here regularly, for something.
The site moves a few feet each year, and nobody has noticed.
A hidden shrine below belongs to a god who still listens.
The real entrance opens only at dawn on the longest day.

Folk in {anchor} swear the people of {name} never age a day past fifty.
A trader came back from {name} with a purse of spirit coins he couldn't explain.
Someone saw lights over {name} three nights running.
They say the well at {name} grants wishes, if you're willing to pay.
A monster bigger than a barn was seen near {name} last month.
The Adventure Society is said to have quietly sent a team to {name}, and they haven't come back.
An outworlder was spotted near {name}, asking strange questions.
There's talk of a lost astral space somewhere near {name}.
They say the Magic Society bought land around {name} for no reason anyone can see.
A girl from {name} turned up in {anchor} with an essence nobody recognised.
The headman of {name} is supposed to be a Silver-ranker in hiding.
They say the {goods} from {name} is cursed this year.
A bandit leader is said to be recruiting in the hills near {name}.
Pilgrims claim that a god spoke at the shrine near {name}.
A merchant offers good money for anything taken from the ruins near {name}.
Someone says the dead walk around {name} on certain nights.
They say {name} pays no taxes, and the lord's collectors keep vanishing on the way.
The children of {name} have been sleepwalking toward the hills.
A great feast is planned in {name}, and everyone's invited.
There's a healer in {name} who can cure anything, but asks a strange price.
