An old adventurer in {name} claims to have a map to a Gold-rank lair.
The river near {name} ran red for a day.
People say the roads near {name} are safer than they've been in years, which is suspicious.
A new church is building a shrine at {name}, and the old shrine-keepers are not happy.
The monsters near {name} have been acting strangely, almost organised.
They say a stranger bought every horse in {name}.
A famous bard is said to be retiring to {name}.
Someone found a monster core the size of a fist in a field near {name}.
The people of {name} are said to be hiding a fugitive.
There's a hermit near {name} who teaches swordsmanship for free.
The water at {name} has started tasting of iron.
A cult is said to be meeting in the woods near {name}.
They say the Adventure Society will open a branch at {name} if it grows.
A caravan was found empty near {name}, horses and all, but no people.
A famous thief is said to have been born in {name}.
They say a rich widow in {name} is looking for a husband, and has buried three.
The harvest at {name} was so good this year that they're giving grain away.
Someone heard singing from the old ruins near {name}.
A boy from {name} joined the Adventure Society and reached Iron rank in a month.
The lord's men are said to be coming to {name} with a list of names.
An earthquake opened a hole near {name}, and something is climbing out.
There's a fortune-teller in {name} who's never wrong.
The innkeeper at {name} is said to have the best wine cellar in the region.
They say the Church of the Healer is quarantining {name}.
Strangers in black have been asking about {name} in {anchor}.
A sea serpent has been seen off the coast near {name}.
They say a forge in {name} makes blades that can cut through monster hide like butter.
A wandering astral space has been seen near {name}.
The people of {name} are said to be preparing for a war.
They say a whole family in {name} vanished overnight.
A merchant claims {name} owes him a fortune.
There's talk of gold in the streams near {name}.
A priest from {name} is said to have performed a real miracle.
A strange sickness is spreading in the flocks near {name}.
They say the old tower near {name} has a new tenant.
The road to {name} is said to be watched by something that isn't human.
Someone in {name} claims to have seen a great astral being.
They say the lord's daughter ran off to {name} with a guard.
An adventuring team from {anchor} is said to be heading for {name}.
The wells near {name} are drying up, and people are blaming witchcraft.
A troupe of travelling players is wintering at {name}.
They say there's a door in a hill near {name} that opens only for the dead.
The famous {goods} from {name} is said to be doubling in price.
A beast-tamer in {name} is said to have a monster that does tricks.
Someone from {name} found an awakening stone in a fish.
They say {name} is built on top of an older town, and you can hear it at night.
A traveller came back from {name} unable to remember the last three days.
The headman of {name} is said to be gravely ill.
Two families in {name} are about to come to blows.
They say the Magic Society tested something near {name} and it went wrong.
A stranger paid for a whole round at {name}'s inn with a gold coin from a forgotten kingdom.
The flowers around {name} bloomed in winter this year.
Someone's been leaving carved wooden animals at doorsteps in {name}.
They say {name} has a secret tunnel to the coast.
A Bronze-rank monster has been sighted near {name}, and nobody's taken the contract.
A child in {name} predicted a storm to the hour.
They say the guard at {name} are taking bribes.
The miller at {name} is said to have struck it rich.
There's a fair at {name} next month with prizes for the best fighters.
They say a giant skeleton was dug up near {name}.
Somebody saw the dead headman of {name} walking on the road.
A messenger from {name} arrived in {anchor} babbling about shadows.
They say the essence users of {name} can talk to animals.
A rich merchant is building a mansion at {name}, and nobody knows why there.
They say someone at {name} is breeding monsters.
There's a market at {name} where you can buy anything, if you know who to ask.
The old bridge near {name} is said to be about to fall.
They say a nest of something has been found under {name}'s granary.
A famous duel will be fought at {name} at the next full moon.
They say people who drink from the spring at {name} dream of the future.
A new road is being cut to {name}, and someone important is paying for it.
They say the scholars at {anchor} are looking for something buried near {name}.
Lights have been seen moving under the lake near {name}.
They say {name} has been offered protection by a house that doesn't usually bother with villages.
A woman from {name} won a fortune at cards in {anchor} and never went home.
They say {name}'s shrine bell rang on its own last week.
The Society's notice board at {anchor} has three contracts posted for {name} this month alone.

problemSettings._about: Regional problems: a kept generated place starts one at this chance; radius in miles; rewards in gp by settlement size (half for places in the outer half of the radius); goodwill lines are offered in turn.
goodwill: Free room and board whenever the party passes through.
The headman spreads the party's name; prices here drop by a tenth.
A local guide offers to take them anywhere nearby, free.
The shrine keeper names them in the prayers for a season.
A family they saved owes them a favour, and means it.
The innkeeper keeps a table for them and the first round is always free.
Word reaches the nearest Adventure Society office, which notes the deed.
Children play at being the party in the square.

sea._about: Places in the water. 'major' and 'minor' kinds become pins on the World map (the Sea places tool; majors are known to players, minors start hidden). 'fleeting' kinds, and now and then a minor kind, are found on ship and sky ship journeys and are only marked if the DM keeps them. where: coast (land within coastMiles), deep (no land within deepMiles) or any. seen: surface, shallow (seen from the air in clear weather only) or sunken (never from the air). explore.cost is the share of a day's travel a diversion takes, before the detour. climate: warm or cold limits a kind by latitude. by: which kinds of travel can find it (ship, air).

major.label: free port isle
descriptions: A rocky island with a deep harbour and a town stacked up the hillside, owing loyalty to no crown on the mainland.
A green island ringed by a sea wall, its harbour crowded with ships from every coast. Customs are whatever the harbour master says they are today.
A low island of salt flats and warehouses, where ships too big for the coastal ports trade cargo at sea prices.
Two islands joined by a stone bridge, one for the town and one for the shipyards, with a lighthouse on the bridge's middle span.

finds: A market where nobody asks where the cargo came from, and a ship's chandler who sells charts of places that aren't on any map.
A notice board at the harbour office with work for adventurers: escorts, salvage, and one unsigned notice offering a great deal of money.
An inn full of sailors who will trade rumours of the open sea for a round of drinks.
A shipyard that can repair anything that floats, and a few things that fly, for a price that depends on how much of a hurry you're in.

secrets: The harbour master answers to a pirate captain who hasn't been seen in person for twenty years.
The isle pays the Church of the Ocean a tithe on every cargo, and ships that don't pay it have a way of not arriving.

major.label: Church of the Journey lighthouse
descriptions: A white tower on a rock, its lamp lit by a spell rather than a flame. Priests of the Church of the Journey keep it, and keep a log of every ship that passes.
A lighthouse built on the back of a sea stack, reached by a stair cut into the rock. Its beam is blue, and ships many miles off steer by it.
A squat stone beacon tower with a chapel at its foot, where sailors leave a coin for a safe crossing.
A lighthouse on a reef, with a small walled harbour where a ship in trouble can shelter from a storm.

finds: The keepers' log, which records every ship that passed for the last forty years, including a few that were never seen again.
A small shrine of the Church of the Journey where travellers can be blessed for the road ahead.
Fresh water, dry beds and news from passing ships.
The keeper, who has seen something out on the water three nights running and wants someone to look into it.

secrets: The lamp's spell draws on a Gold-rank core sealed in the tower's foundation, and someone has worked out how to steal it.
One of the keepers has been dimming the lamp on certain nights, for wreckers who pay well.

major.label: maelstrom
descriptions: A whirlpool a mile across, its roar heard long before it is seen. It never stops, not even in a dead calm.
A great slow spiral of water with a dark eye at its centre, where the sea seems to drain away into nothing.
A whirlpool that turns the wrong way for this half of the world, ringed by floating wreckage that has been going round for years.
A churning patch of sea where three currents meet and fight. Ships that stray in come out somewhere else, or not at all.

finds: Wreckage circling on the outer edge, some of it with cargo still lashed down.
A glimpse, at the eye, of stonework far below: steps going down.
Water monsters that feed on whatever the whirl drags in, and are very used to easy meals.
A ship's figurehead caught on the rim, carved with the name of a ship lost a century ago.
explore.check: DC 15 Wisdom (Survival) or Dexterity check with water vehicles to hold the ship on the rim

secrets: The maelstrom is the drain of an astral space beneath the sea, and it is slowly filling.
Something at the eye is turning it, and it is getting tired.

major.label: sunken city
descriptions: The roofs and towers of a drowned city just under the surface, clear as glass on a calm day. Fish swim through its windows.
A city that slid into the sea in a single night, its streets now ten fathoms down. At low tide the tallest tower breaks the surface.
Columns and domes under green water, too big to have been built by the people who live on this coast now.
A harbour town on a sunken shelf, its walls still standing, its bell still in the tower.

finds: A sealed vault in what was once a counting house, still dry inside.
A temple of a god nobody worships any more, its altar furred with coral.
Merfolk salvagers who think of the city as theirs.
Statues of the city's founders, one of them clutching a bronze box.
explore.check: DC 13 Strength (Athletics) to dive, or water breathing

secrets: The city didn't sink. It was pulled down, by something its rulers made a bargain with.
The people of the city are still there, in an astral space that opened as the water came in.

major.label: astral space on a reef
descriptions: A reef in a perfect circle, with a shimmer at its centre where the water does not quite meet the sky. It is the entrance to an astral space.
Coral that glows at night around an astral space entrance just under the surface. The Adventure Society has marked it with a buoy.
A ring of black rock around a pool of still water in the middle of the open sea: an astral space, and an old one.
A reef where the fish are all the wrong colours, around a doorway into an astral space that only opens on the ebb tide.

finds: The entrance to the astral space, and the marks of the last team that went in.
An Adventure Society buoy with a sealed tube holding the last team's report.
Monster cores washed up on the coral, from things that came out.
A stranded team of Iron-rankers who went in and came back out without their boat.

secrets: The astral space is leaking: its monsters have started to breed in the reef.
A faction has been using the astral space to hide something, and its guards are not far away.

major.label: leviathan's bones
descriptions: The ribs of a leviathan rise out of the sea like the beams of a burnt hall, white and huge. Birds nest in them.
A skull the size of a castle, half sunk, its eye sockets big enough to sail a boat through.
The spine of some sea titan, curving out of the water for half a mile, slowly being crusted over by coral.
A leviathan carcass, still fresh enough to stink for miles, with monsters of every size feeding on it.

finds: Monster cores of every rank lodged in the bone, some of them high.
Scavengers that do not want to share.
The wound that killed the leviathan: something bigger bit it.
A hollow in the skull where a hermit has made a home.

secrets: The leviathan was killed by a Diamond-ranker, who left the bones as a warning to something else.
Its young are still alive, and they come back to the bones every spring.

major.label: pirate haven
descriptions: A cove hidden behind a sea stack, with ships at anchor and a shanty town on stilts above the waterline.
A fortified rock with cannons, or something like them, pointing out to sea, flying no flag at all.
A sunken ship's hulk turned into a tavern and market, run by a crew that has given up honest work.
An island with a lookout tower on every headland and a harbour you can only enter if you know the channel.

finds: A tavern where captains sell their services, and buy information.
A prison cell with a captured merchant who will pay well to be rescued.
Charts of the shipping lanes, marked with which ships pay for safe passage.
A council of captains who would rather hire the party than fight them.

secrets: The pirates are paid by a noble house on the mainland to raid its rivals.
The haven's leader is an essence user of a higher rank than anyone else here suspects.

major.label: floating market
descriptions: Hundreds of boats lashed together into a floating town that drifts with the currents, trading as it goes.
A raft city built on the backs of sleeping sea turtles the size of islands. Nobody remembers when they last woke.
Barges and hulks chained in a great ring around a market barge, where anything can be bought for the right coin.
A floating market on rafts of woven reed and cork, run by sea folk who rarely set foot on land.

finds: A market where spirit coins, pearls and monster cores are all good money.
A trader with an awakening stone they found in a fish.
A floating shrine to the Church of the Ocean, where the priests read the currents.
News from every coast the raft has drifted past this year.

secrets: The market is the way a smuggling ring moves cargo between kingdoms that have banned it.
The raft's elders steer it, and they are steering it towards something.

major.label: endless storm
descriptions: A storm that never moves and never ends, a black wall of cloud on the horizon lit from inside by lightning.
A ring of storms around a patch of calm sea, which sailors say is the eye of a god's anger.
Lightning that strikes the same stretch of sea over and over, boiling it, under a sky that is clear everywhere else.
A storm that walks, slowly, in a circle a hundred miles across, as it has done for as long as there have been charts.

finds: A calm eye at the centre, with a small island no one has ever landed on.
Storm elementals that do not like visitors.
Lightning-struck glass in the shallows, prized by mages.
A wrecked sky ship, still crackling with stored power.
explore.check: DC 15 Wisdom (Survival) to find a way through the squalls

secrets: The storm was raised by the Church of the Storm to hide something, and the church has forgotten what.
The storm is a creature, and it is asleep.

major.label: merfolk outpost
descriptions: Coral towers just under the surface, grown into shape by merfolk, with a trading platform built above them where surface folk are allowed.
A merfolk town in a lagoon, its bubble-houses glowing at night, its people curious about anyone who comes in peace.
A merfolk watch post on a reef, guarding the way to somewhere deeper they will not talk about.
A kelp forest grown into avenues and halls, the summer court of a merfolk noble family.

finds: Merfolk traders who swap pearls and sea-silk for iron and books.
A merfolk envoy with a problem only surface folk can solve.
Coral grown into weapons and armour, for those the merfolk trust.
Old treaties carved in stone, which the nearest kingdom has forgotten it signed.

secrets: The outpost is spying on the shipping lanes for a merfolk queen who is thinking about war.
The merfolk here have been trading with the Church of Purity, and are frightened of them.

major.label: smoking island
descriptions: A volcanic island that smokes day and night, its black beaches steaming where the waves meet them.
A new island, a few years old, still rising from the sea in fits of fire and ash.
A ring of volcanic rock with a lake of fire at its heart, where fire-essence users come on pilgrimage.
A volcano whose lava runs into the sea in glowing rivers, with a monastery perched on its cold side.

finds: Obsidian and fire-touched stone worth a lot to crafters.
Fire monsters that nest in the warm rock.
A hot spring where wounds heal faster.
A smith who works with lava, and takes commissions.

secrets: The volcano is a sealed astral space under pressure, and it will burst.
Something sleeps in the magma chamber, and the eruptions are it turning over.

major.label: Magic Society sea station
descriptions: A tower on stilts in the open sea, run by the Magic Society to study the currents of mana in the deep water.
A platform anchored over a trench, its scholars lowering instruments into the dark on chains a mile long.
A domed station on a rock, where Magic Society mages watch the stars, the tides and the things that rise between them.
A cluster of glass domes floating on cork rafts, growing strange plants in sea water for the Magic Society.

finds: Scholars who will pay for samples from the deep.
Records of every monster sighted in these waters.
An experiment that has got out of hand.
A library of sea charts more accurate than any on the mainland.

secrets: The station is listening for something in the deep, and it has started answering.
Its head mage has been selling the Society's findings to a rival guild.

major.label: drowned temple
descriptions: The roof of a temple shows above the waves at low tide, its doors facing down into the sea.
A temple of the Church of the Ocean built under the water on purpose, where priests go down to pray in bubbles of air.
A temple to a god that no longer exists, sunk as punishment, its bells still ringing when the currents move them.
Pillars marching out into the sea from a beach, ending at a temple that is only dry on one night a year.

finds: Offerings left by sailors for a hundred years.
A priest of the Church of the Ocean keeping a vigil.
A divine relic, and the guardian that came with it.
Murals showing the coast as it was before the sea came in.
explore.check: DC 13 Strength (Athletics) to swim down to the doors

secrets: The temple's god is not as dead as people think, and it is hungry.
The Church of the Ocean drowned this temple, and doesn't want anyone to know why.

major.label: monster breeding grounds
descriptions: Stretch of sea where the water boils with feeding things, and every sailor knows to steer wide.
The spawning grounds of a sea monster, its eggs floating in great rafts of slime on the surface.
A kraken's hunting ground, marked on the charts with a drawing of tentacles and the word 'no'.
Waters where sea serpents gather to fight over mates once a year, and are short-tempered the rest of it.

finds: Monster eggs, worth a fortune to the right buyer and death to the wrong one.
A wrecked whaling ship, its harpoons still loaded.
Shed scales and teeth that crafters will pay for.
The thing itself, and it is awake.

secrets: The monsters are being bred, deliberately, by someone with an essence that lets them talk to sea beasts.
The brood mother is old and dying, and her young will scatter along the coast when she does.

major.label: ship graveyard
descriptions: A sea of floating weed so thick a ship can stick fast in it, dotted with the hulks of ships that did.
Dead water where the wind never blows, full of the masts of becalmed and abandoned ships.
A tangle of wreckage held together by weed, so big that people live on it, scavenging what drifts in.
A place where the currents bring every wreck in this ocean, eventually.

finds: A ship's hold full of cargo nobody came back for.
Weed-folk scavengers who know every hulk by name.
The log of a captain who got out, and the way she did it.
Something in the weed that moves when the party moves.
explore.check: DC 14 Wisdom (Survival) to steer clear of the thickest weed on the way out

secrets: The weed is one living thing, and it decides who leaves.
One of the hulks is a treasure ship that three navies are still looking for.

major.label: island in the mist
descriptions: An island that is only there in the fog. Sailors who land find it inhabited, and the people are always very pleased to see them.
A mist that hangs over one patch of sea even on a bright day, hiding an island with a ruined palace.
An island on every old chart and none of the new ones, which some ships still find.
Grey cliffs that appear out of the fog and vanish when the wind changes, with lights in windows high up.

finds: A palace where time runs differently.
Islanders who ask the party to stay, and mean it.
A way off the island that does not come back to the same sea.
An archive of everyone who has ever landed here.

secrets: The island is an astral space that has drifted out into the world, and it is lonely.
The islanders are the crew of the first ship that found it, and they cannot leave.

major.label: sea fortress
descriptions: A fortress on a rock in the mouth of a strait, its towers commanding the sea lanes for miles.
An old naval fort, half abandoned, now garrisoned by a handful of soldiers who haven't been paid in a year.
A sea wall a mile long with a fort at each end, built to keep something out of the bay.
An Adventure Society outpost in an old fort, watching the waters for monsters coming inshore.

finds: Soldiers who want news, supplies and someone to listen to their complaints.
An armoury that hasn't been inventoried in years.
Contracts posted by the Adventure Society for sea monsters in the area.
A captain who will let the party pass for a favour.

secrets: The fort's guns are for show; its real defence was a ward that failed last winter.
The garrison has been taking bribes to let a particular ship through.

minor.label: shipwreck
descriptions: The ribs of a wrecked ship on a reef, its mast still standing at an angle.
A merchant ship broken on rocks, its stern under water and its bow still dry.
A wreck sitting upright on a sandbank, as if it had been set down there gently.
The hull of an old warship, crusted with barnacles, its name long worn away.

finds: Cargo in the dry part of the hold.
The captain's strongbox, wedged under a beam.
Something living in the wreck now.
A ship's log that ends mid-sentence.
explore.check: DC 12 Strength (Athletics) to get into the flooded hold

minor.label: islet
descriptions: A small island with a spring of fresh water and a few trees bent by the wind.
A sandy cay barely higher than the waves, with turtle tracks up the beach.
A green islet with a ruined hut and a cairn on its highest point.
A rocky island covered in nesting birds, loud enough to hear a mile off.

finds: Fresh water and fruit, and a day's rest.
A cairn with a message in it from the last people who landed.
A castaway, who may or may not want rescuing.
A buried chest, badly buried.

minor.label: sandbar
descriptions: A long sandbar that shows at low tide, with the masts of ships that didn't see it in time.
A shoal of white sand in the middle of the sea, glaringly bright, with seals basking on it.
A bank of shifting sand that is never in the same place twice on the charts.

finds: Wreckage and flotsam washed up at the tideline.
A seal colony that is not as friendly as it looks.
Footprints, fresh, of something that walked up out of the sea and back in.

minor.label: sea stack
descriptions: A pillar of rock standing alone in the sea, taller than a tower, with a nest at the top.
A sea stack carved by the waves into the shape of a face looking out to sea.
Three needles of rock in a row, which sailors call the Sisters and salute as they pass.

finds: A giant bird's nest at the top, with eggs.
Carvings near the waterline, old and worn.
A cave at the base, reached only at low tide.

minor.label: kelp forest
descriptions: Great kelp forest swaying just under the surface, so thick a rowboat can barely push through.
A forest of kelp with stalks as thick as trees, where the light comes down in green beams.
Kelp that glows faintly at night, drawing fish, and the things that eat fish.

finds: Sea otters who have learned to steal from boats.
A merfolk hunting party.
A drowned boat tangled in the kelp, with a body still at the oars.

minor.label: glowing shoals
descriptions: Shallow water that glows blue at night, so bright you could read by it.
A patch of sea full of tiny lights that swirl around anything that moves through the water.
Shoals where the fish shine like lanterns, and the fishermen come out at night to net them.

finds: Glowing fish whose scales alchemists will buy.
A spot where the lights spell out something, if you watch from above.
A strong mana current: essence abilities feel sharper here.

minor.label: sea cave
descriptions: A sea cave in a cliff, its mouth only open at low tide.
A grotto where the waves boom in and out like breathing.
A cave behind a waterfall that falls straight into the sea.

finds: A smuggler's stash.
A pool at the back with something living in it.
Old paintings on the walls, of ships no one builds any more.
explore.check: DC 12 Wisdom (Survival) to time the tide

minor.label: sea shrine
descriptions: A stone shrine of the Church of the Ocean on a tiny rock, where passing ships leave offerings.
A floating shrine on a raft anchored in deep water, with a bell that rings in the swell.
A wayside shrine of the Church of the Journey on a buoy, with a lamp that never goes out.

finds: Offerings of coins and food, which it would be very unlucky to take.
A priest who comes out once a month to tend it, and is overdue.
A blessing for the voyage, if the party pays its respects.

minor.label: smugglers' rock
descriptions: A bare rock with an iron ring set into it, where ships meet to swap cargo out of sight of the customs.
A rock with a cleft that hides a cache, marked with a scratch only smugglers know to look for.
A ledge where boats tie up at night, and nobody is ever seen there by day.

finds: A cache of contraband waiting to be collected.
Smugglers waiting for a boat that is late.
A note giving the time and place of the next drop.

minor.label: abandoned fishing platform
descriptions: A fishing platform on stilts far from shore, its huts empty and its nets rotting.
A whaling station on pilings, abandoned in a hurry, the pots still on the fires.
A pearl-divers' platform with its ladders pulled up, as if whoever was there didn't want anything following them.

finds: Signs of what made the fishers leave.
Tools and stores worth taking.
A survivor, hiding.

minor.label: whale fall
descriptions: The body of a great whale floating belly-up, birds and sharks feeding on it.
A whale's bones on the bottom of a shallow bank, a feast for everything in the sea.
A dead sea beast, still warm, with a harpoon in it that isn't from any whaler.

finds: Ambergris worth a small fortune.
The monster core, if someone gets to it before the sharks.
Whatever killed it, still nearby.

minor.label: pearl beds
descriptions: Oyster beds in warm shallows, with pearl divers' marker floats bobbing over them.
A bank of giant clams, some of them big enough to hide a person.
Pearl beds the merfolk say belong to them.

finds: Pearls, for anyone who dives for them.
A giant clam that closes on a diver's foot.
Divers who say the beds are theirs and want a cut.
explore.check: DC 12 Strength (Athletics) to dive for pearls

minor.label: hot spring vent
descriptions: A patch of sea that steams and bubbles, warm as a bath, smelling of sulphur.
Hot springs on the sea floor, ringed by strange white crabs and pale weed.
A vent that throws up a spout of steam every hour, regular as a bell.

finds: Minerals that crust the rocks, prized by alchemists.
Warm water where fire-essence users feel very at home.
Creatures that live in the heat and nowhere else.

minor.label: drowned causeway
descriptions: A paved road running out into the sea, under the water, going somewhere that is no longer there.
Stepping stones across a strait, only above water at the lowest tides.
The arches of an ancient bridge, the middle spans long fallen.

finds: Milestones in a language no one speaks.
A toll house at the end, half sunk, with its coffers still locked.
A sense of being watched from the far end of the road.

minor.label: tower in the sea
descriptions: A stone tower standing straight up out of the sea, with no island under it and no door above the waterline.
A wizard's tower on a rock barely big enough to hold it, its windows shuttered.
A watchtower from a war no one remembers, still with a flag on top that is changed by someone.

finds: A door below the waterline.
The tower's owner, who doesn't get many visitors.
A spellbook left open on a desk.

minor.label: coral garden
descriptions: A reef of coral in every colour, grown into shapes too regular to be natural.
A coral garden tended by merfolk, with paths between the beds.
Coral that has grown over a wreck in the shape of the ship.

finds: Coral that someone with a water or life essence could grow into anything.
A merfolk gardener who is not happy about boats.
A creature that lives in the coral and looks just like it.

minor.label: sunken statue
descriptions: A giant statue standing on the sea floor, its head and raised hand above the water.
A stone face as big as a house, looking up from the shallows.
A statue of a sea god, toppled and lying under clear water.

finds: A hollow in the statue's head.
An inscription naming who made it, and why.
Offerings tucked into cracks.

minor.label: bell rock
descriptions: A rock with a great bronze bell hung on an iron frame, rung by the waves to warn ships off.
A reef with a bell buoy that rings even when the sea is flat.
A rock where a bell can be heard, but no bell can be seen.

finds: Whoever keeps the bell in repair.
A ghost who rings it.
Wreckage of the ships that didn't listen.

minor.label: hermit's island
descriptions: A tiny island with one stone house and a garden, and smoke from the chimney.
A rock with a hut built from driftwood, and a person sitting on the step watching the sea.
An island where an old adventurer went to be left alone.

finds: A hermit who knows these waters better than anyone.
A retired adventurer of high rank, who does not want to be found.
A garden of herbs that grow nowhere else.

minor.label: seal rocks
descriptions: Rocks crowded with seals, barking at every ship that passes.
A colony of sea lions on a flat skerry, guarded by a huge old bull.
Ledges where seals come ashore, and where people say some of the seals take off their skins at night.

finds: Seals that are not all seals.
Fishermen who want the colony culled.
A pup tangled in a net.

minor.label: core reef
descriptions: A reef where monster cores have settled over centuries, glinting through the water.
A shelf of rock where mana pools, and small sea monsters spawn and die by the hundred.
A reef that grew around a broken astral space, spawning monsters from the water itself.

finds: Monster cores lying loose on the reef.
Fresh spawns that are hostile and hungry.
A mana current strong enough to make essence abilities hard to control.

minor.label: iceberg
descriptions: An iceberg the size of a town, blue at the waterline.
A drifting floe with something dark frozen in its heart.
Ice cliffs rising out of the fog, calving with a sound like thunder.

finds: Something frozen in the ice, not quite dead.
A cave in the ice with a camp in it.
Seals, bears and the things that eat them.

minor.label: standing stones on a skerry
descriptions: A circle of standing stones on a skerry barely above the waves.
A single tall stone on a rock, carved with spirals.
Stones that hum in a storm.

finds: A ritual site still in use.
Carvings that map the stars.
A buried urn.

minor.label: stilt hamlet
descriptions: A cluster of fishers' huts on stilts in a shallow bay, joined by rope bridges.
A hamlet built on an old breakwater, its people half in the sea.
A floating village of houseboats moored together, moving with the fish.

finds: Fresh fish, gossip and a place to sleep.
Fishers with a problem in the water.
A healer who works with sea plants.

minor.label: sky ship wreck
descriptions: A sky ship floating upside down in the sea, kept up by what's left of its lift crystals.
The wreck of a cloud house, slowly dissolving into mist on the water.
A sky ship's gondola caught on a reef, its balloon long gone.

finds: Lift crystals, still working, worth a fortune.
The crew's last message.
Whatever brought it down.

minor.label: old sea wall
descriptions: A ruined breakwater far from any harbour, the harbour it sheltered long gone.
A pier running out from nowhere into deep water.
An old sea wall with gates in it, though there is nothing behind them but more sea.

finds: Mooring rings and a place to shelter.
A plaque naming a city that is not on any map.
A sealed cistern still full of fresh water.

fleeting.label: ghost ship
descriptions: A ship with grey sails and no crew in sight, sailing against the wind.
A ship from a hundred years ago, lights in its cabins, music playing aboard.
A pale ship that keeps pace with the party's, a mile off, no matter what they do.

finds: A crew of ghosts reliving their last night.
A cabin with a letter addressed to someone the party knows.
A hold full of cargo that turns to sand by morning.

fleeting.label: sleeping turtle
descriptions: An island with trees and a beach that is moving, slowly, against the current.
A great turtle asleep on the surface, its shell grown over with a small forest.

finds: A tiny island ecosystem on the shell, with fruit.
A barnacle-crusted chest wedged in the shell.
The turtle waking up.

fleeting.label: castaways on a raft
descriptions: A raft with people on it, waving a shirt on an oar.
Survivors clinging to a broken hatch cover.
A lifeboat with three people in it, one of them not moving.

finds: Sailors from a ship that went down two days ago, and what sank it.
A merchant who will pay well for rescue, and better for silence.
A survivor who is not what they seem.

fleeting.label: drifting cargo
descriptions: Crates bobbing in the water, a long line of them, from a ship that lost its deck cargo.
A chest floating on its own, sealed with wax.
Barrels lashed together, drifting.

finds: Trade goods, still dry.
A sealed chest with a curse on the lock.
Something that knocks from inside.

fleeting.label: a sea serpent's shed skin
descriptions: A sea serpent's shed skin, a hundred yards long, floating like a ribbon of glass.

finds: Scales that crafters will pay well for.
The serpent, not far away and touchy after moulting.

fleeting.label: whales in trouble
descriptions: A pod of whales circling a calf caught in a net.
Whales singing at the ship, as if asking for something.

finds: A calf to free, and grateful whales.
A poacher's net with a mark on it.
A whale that leads the party somewhere.

fleeting.label: waterspout
descriptions: A waterspout dancing across the sea, with something caught in it, spinning.
Three waterspouts in a row, moving together in a way storms shouldn't.

finds: Something that falls out when the spout breaks.
Storm elementals at play.
explore.check: DC 13 Wisdom (Survival) to get close safely

fleeting.label: mana surge
descriptions: A patch of sea that glows and shimmers with raw mana, the air above it crackling.
Water that has gone perfectly still and mirror-bright, with a hum in it.

finds: Monsters spawning out of the water as the party watches.
An awakening stone forming in the heart of it.
A burst of mana that leaves everyone's abilities stronger for an hour.

fleeting.label: ship in distress
descriptions: A merchant ship with a broken mast, flying a distress flag.
A ship on fire, its crew in the water.
A fishing boat being circled by something under the water.

finds: A crew who will owe the party a favour.
Pirates pretending to be in trouble.
Cargo that someone wants back.

fleeting.label: dead sea monster
descriptions: A sea monster floating dead, its belly to the sky, its core still in it.
Two sea monsters locked together in death, drifting.

finds: A monster core, and maybe an essence.
Scavengers who got there first.
Whatever killed it.

fleeting.label: fog bank with voices
descriptions: A wall of fog on the water, and voices in it, calling names.
A fog bank that drifts towards the ship against the wind.

finds: Ghosts of the drowned who want a message carried home.
A lost ship, and a way out for it.
Something that learned to mimic voices.

fleeting.label: dolphins leading the way
descriptions: A pod of dolphins playing at the bow, then swimming off and coming back, as if to show the way.

finds: A wreck the dolphins want found.
A person in the water, alive.
A merfolk messenger.

fleeting.label: astral space breaching
descriptions: A shimmering dome rising out of the sea: an astral space surfacing for a few hours.
A hole in the water that doesn't fill, with light coming up from it.

finds: An astral space that will close by nightfall, with anyone still inside.
Monsters coming out of it.
Treasure on the threshold.

fleeting.label: sky ship in trouble
descriptions: A sky ship losing height, smoke trailing from its lift chamber.
A cloud house drifting low over the water, its owners signalling for help.

finds: A crew who need lift crystals or a mage.
A noble passenger with enemies.
Cargo they'd rather dump than explain.

fleeting.label: burning water
descriptions: A slick of oil on the sea, burning, with something swimming in the flames.

finds: A fire elemental, lost and angry.
The wreck that spilled the oil.

fleeting.label: message in a bottle
descriptions: A bottle with a message, bobbing past.
A sealed glass float with a map rolled up inside.

finds: A map to a place in these waters.
A plea for help from somewhere years ago.
A love letter, and a name.

fleeting.label: sea monsters fighting
descriptions: Two great sea monsters fighting, the sea boiling around them.
A kraken and a whale locked together, rolling.

finds: The winner, wounded and dangerous.
The loser's core, sinking.

fleeting.label: floating ruin
descriptions: A chunk of a tower floating like a cork, enchanted to never sink.
A floating garden island, broken off something much bigger.

finds: Rooms still furnished and dry.
An enchantment worth studying.
A guardian still on duty.

fleeting.label: something frozen in the ice
descriptions: A small iceberg with a shape inside it, dark and still.

finds: A creature from another age.
A person, perfectly preserved, with a strange essence.

fleeting.label: lights under the water
descriptions: Lights moving under the water, in formation, below the ship.
A glow far below, as if a city were lit at the bottom of the sea.

finds: Merfolk travelling in a procession.
Something huge, bioluminescent, rising.
A sunken place that is not on any chart.

secrets: Smugglers use it as a meeting point, and leave a lantern in a particular place when a drop is due.
A pod of merfolk keep watch here for their queen, and report on every ship.
It sits on top of a sealed astral space, and the seal is weakening.
A Silver-rank sea monster sleeps nearby, and noise wakes it.
A noble house on the mainland claims it, with papers no one has checked in a century.
Something here is worth a great deal to the Magic Society, and they don't know it is here.
The Church of the Ocean considers it sacred, and punishes those who take from it.
A treasure was hidden here by a pirate who is still alive and still coming back for it.
Its waters carry a faint curse: anyone who takes something away has bad luck at sea until they bring it back.
A cult has been leaving offerings here for something that lives in the deep.
The currents here lead straight to somewhere else in the world, for anything that floats.
An outworlder washed up here years ago and left a journal no one could read.
rumours: Sailors say lights have been seen around {name} on moonless nights.
A fishing boat came back from near {name} with nets full of fish that had never been seen before.
They say a ship's bell can be heard at {name} when a storm is coming.
A captain in {anchor} swears she saw a woman walking on the water near {name}.
The charts in {anchor} mark {name} with a warning, and nobody remembers why.
Someone in {anchor} is quietly hiring divers to go to {name}.
A merfolk trader said the sea around {name} has gone quiet, and the fish have left.
They say {name} moves, a little, every year.
A sky ship crew saw something big under the water near {name}.
The Adventure Society in {anchor} has stopped sending Iron-rankers anywhere near {name}.

twists._about: What can go wrong when the party diverts to explore a sea place. chance: how often something does, by the Travel tab's Exploring setting (a kind's explore.danger nudges it up or down). weights: how likely each sort is (fight and hazard grow with the kind's danger). {dc}, {dmg} and {half} scale with the party's rank; {place} is what the place is (a shipwreck, a sea cave). lose: extra share of the day lost (a hazard's only on a failed check). seen limits a hazard to places that are on the surface, shallow or sunken. In a dilemma, each choice says whether the party still gets the loot.

Another crew had the same idea, got here first, and isn't in the mood to share.
What they came for has a guardian, and it wakes the moment anyone gets close.

dilemmas.text: Someone is here: half-starved, sunburnt, and wearing the brand of an escaped convict. They beg the party not to tell anyone.

choices.label: Take them along
choices.text: They are grateful and useful, but a bounty hunter may come asking questions later.

choices.label: Hand them in
choices.text: The bounty is the party's reward. The convict swears they were innocent, and they may be telling the truth.

choices.label: Leave them be
choices.text: The party leaves food and walks away. Nobody will thank them for it, either way.

dilemmas.text: The valuables are wrapped in letters: the crew's wages, meant for their families back in port.

choices.label: Keep it
choices.text: The coin is the party's. If word gets out, sailors in that port won't forget it.

choices.label: Take it to the families
choices.text: No loot, but the families and their port remember the party kindly.

dilemmas.text: A big creature has made a nest here, with young. It watches the party but hasn't attacked. Its cores would be worth a lot.

choices.label: Kill it for the cores
choices.text: A fight, and the young are left to fend for themselves. The cores are the reward.

choices.label: Leave it be
choices.text: The party backs away with nothing. Some druid, priest or sailor may hear of it and think better of them.

dilemmas.text: Another crew got here first and is in trouble: their boat holed and the water rising. Saving them means leaving the prize for the sea.

choices.label: Save them
choices.text: No loot, but the crew owes the party a favour, and sailors talk.

choices.label: Grab the prize
choices.text: The party gets the prize. Some of the crew may not make it, and those who do will remember.

dilemmas.text: The prize turns out to be offerings at a little shrine, left by fishing families for luck at sea.

choices.label: Take the offerings
choices.text: The coin is the party's. Superstitious sailors will call it bad luck, and maybe they are right.

choices.label: Leave them, and add one
choices.text: No loot. A small offering of their own buys a calm sea for the next day, or so the locals would say.

dilemmas.text: A trapped spirit speaks to them from the {place}. It offers to tell them where something far better is hidden, if they break the binding that holds it. The binding was put there on purpose.

choices.label: Free it
choices.text: It keeps its word, and the party gets the loot. What it does with its freedom is another story.

choices.label: Leave it bound
choices.text: No loot. The spirit curses them as they go, and it has a long memory.

dilemmas.text: The cargo is contraband: stolen goods, or essences someone shouldn't have. Whoever stashed it will come back for it.

choices.label: Take it
choices.text: The party gets the loot, and the smugglers may come looking for whoever took it.

choices.label: Report it
choices.text: No loot, but the authorities in the next port are grateful, and might pay a reward of their own.

choices.label: Leave it
choices.text: Not their problem. Nothing gained, nothing owed.

dilemmas.text: A dying sailor is here, and with their last strength asks the party to carry a sealed letter to someone in port. It is out of the way.

choices.label: Promise to deliver it
choices.text: The party takes the letter. Whoever gets it in port will be grateful, and the letter may matter more than anyone knows.

choices.label: Refuse
choices.text: The sailor dies without hope. The party takes what it found.

dilemmas.text: The prize is beautiful, and everyone who touches it hears a whisper they can't quite make out.

choices.label: Take it anyway
choices.text: The party gets the loot, and whatever is whispering comes with it.

choices.label: Leave it
choices.text: No loot. The whispering stops the moment they let go.

dilemmas.text: Among the finds is proof that a well-known merchant house sank this ship on purpose, crew and all.

choices.label: Take the proof to the authorities
choices.text: The party keeps the loot and makes a powerful enemy, and some powerful friends.

choices.label: Keep it, for leverage
choices.text: Blackmail material. Dangerous to hold and worth a lot to the right buyer.

choices.label: Burn it
choices.text: Nobody will ever know. The party keeps the loot.

dilemmas.text: Seals, birds or dolphins are caught in an old net here, dying slowly.

choices.label: Cut them free
choices.text: It takes hours, and the animals are grateful in the way animals are.

choices.label: Take what they came for
choices.text: The party gets the loot and leaves them. Nobody saw, except the animals.

dilemmas.text: A frightened child is hiding here. They say their family went into the water to look for something and never came up.

choices.label: Search for the family
choices.text: The party loses the rest of the day searching. What they find is up to the DM.

choices.label: Take the child to port
choices.text: The child comes with the party. Someone in port will know them.

dilemmas.text: A captive is tied up here, and says the pirates who left them will be back by nightfall. They also say they know where the pirates keep their share.

choices.label: Free them
choices.text: They lead the party to the stash, but the pirates will know who did it, and may come for them.

choices.label: Leave them
choices.text: The party gets away clean, with nothing from the stash.

dilemmas.text: Merfolk or sea people hold this place sacred, and one of them is watching. Taking anything here is theft, by their law.

choices.label: Take it anyway
choices.text: The party gets the loot, and the sea people of these waters won't welcome them again.

choices.label: Ask permission
choices.text: A DC {dc} Charisma (Persuasion) check: on a success they may take a little (the loot), and on a failure they leave with nothing but the sea people's respect.

choices.label: Leave it
choices.text: No loot, and the watcher nods as they go.

The boat scrapes a rock on the way in, and patching it costs hours.
